A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new construction of a hash-function-based PRG that relies on a collision-resistant hash function and on a worst-case regularity assumption.

, given a family of functions that are regular in the sense of worst-case regularity and collision-resistant (in the exponential sense), we can construct a PRG with a short seed that is computationally indistinguishable from a truly random generator.
we present a pseudorandom generator that relies on a collision-resistant hash function and is secure up to the birthday bound.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the security of a PRG based on a regular hash function is not limited to the security of the underlying function.
collision-resistance, which is a stronger assumption than one-wayness and is believed to be harder to achieve, can be sufficient to build a PRG.
collision resistance is a strong enough assumption for the purpose of pseudorandomness.
